text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Opposition party Christian Democrats made their first moves to revive the party' parliamentary group that was dissolved last week.
- Conservative parties have to unite ahead of next year's elections, an official of opposition Democratic People's Party said.
- Romanian extremists support the man who stole the Romanian flag from Hungary's recently opened consulate in Cluj.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Hungary has been waiting for two years for Slovakia to sign a defense agreement, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- The Finnish-Japanese consortium IVO-Tomen plans to spend 20 billion forints on the reconstruction and expansion of the Ujpest power plant.
- IAS figures showed that POstabank made a loss of 109 million forints in 1996.
- ING Bank and Dunabank have violated the laws on data protection and financial institutions, ombudsman Laszlo Majtenyi said.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Croatian Privatisation Fund has refused oil and gas company MOL's bid to buy a 12.5 percent stake in the Adriatic pipeline.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Spring frosts have reduced this year's fruit crop by 10 to 30 percent compared with last year.
- Heavy rains have deteriorated the quality of Hungary's wheat crop.
- The reduction of government projects will save four billion forints for the budget.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Foreign direct investment in the January-May period was $1 billion , up from $406 million in the same period of last year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Citibank posted a 2.65 billion forints net profit in the first half of 1996.
